transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net customer billing, my name is Ian. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Ian. I'm looking closely at my monthly itemized bill and I've been charged twenty-four pounds for extra mobile data, but I was told repeatedly that my tariff had an automatic data cap.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand your concern about unexpected data charges on your monthly invoice, Mason. Let me look directly into your tariff details and see why that charge applied.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks, I really appreciate you checking because I always keep the safety buffer turned on.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we access your billing records, Mason, could you verify your home address and your four-digit account security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 19 Cambridge Road, Oxford, OX4 1EP, the account security PIN is 5192, and the mobile phone line with the charge is zero seven seven zero zero, nine zero zero four five two.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for verifying those details, Mason. I have your account pulled up on our billing system.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great, thanks for getting that open so fast.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So just to confirm what you're seeing on your online billing portal: your latest statement shows an additional twenty-four pounds in out-of-plan mobile data usage, but you expected your monthly spend cap to prevent any extra charges. Have I got that completely right?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exactly. I have a ten-gigabyte plan and I assumed it just slowed down or stopped once I hit ten gigabytes.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me check the detailed data usage logs for that billing cycle. The statement period ran from the third of last month to the second of this month.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Okay, what do the daily logs show?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: On the twenty-second of last month, our network traffic monitor recorded a continuous data session of six gigabytes over about four hours between seven in the evening and eleven at night.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Ah, my home broadband was being upgraded that evening so I was streaming an important football match on my laptop using my mobile phone hotspot.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Hotspot video streaming on a high-definition laptop screen consumes roughly 1.5 gigabytes per hour, which quickly pushed your total consumption to 14.8 gigabytes.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Right, but shouldn't the spend cap have kicked in at zero pounds extra?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Checking your profile settings on our provisioning server... when your account migrated to our new billing platform in March, the default spend cap was unfortunately reset to thirty pounds rather than zero.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Nobody told me it changed to thirty pounds when you moved platforms! I never agreed to that change, and charging me twenty-four pounds for an internal system glitch is completely unfair and frustrating!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I completely understand why that's frustrating, Mason, especially when you believed the cap was still locked firmly at zero. Let me see how we can rectify this for you right away.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Ian, because twenty-four pounds extra is quite a lot of unexpected money for an error during a platform switch.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Because that spend cap threshold reverted during our internal systems migration without your explicit consent, you should certainly not be penalized for that charge on your statement.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can you credit the twenty-four pounds back to my account?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, I have full supervisory authorization to issue a direct credit of twenty-four pounds to your billing ledger.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is fantastic news. Does that credit come off my next direct debit automatically without any paperwork?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, your next monthly direct debit will automatically be reduced by exactly twenty-four pounds on collection day.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's very fair of you, thank you.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now let's look at why your data didn't pause automatically when you hit your allowance.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does the system send an alert when you hit eighty percent?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, our automated system normally sends an SMS notification at eighty percent and one hundred percent usage.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I didn't receive any text message on the twenty-second.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Checking the notification dispatch queue... the SMS alert was queued behind an exchange gateway maintenance window that evening.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So the warning text arrived hours after the match had finished.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That explains why you had no real-time indication that your data allowance had been exhausted.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'm glad you can see that on your audit logs.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now let's lock your spend cap permanently to zero pounds so no future out-of-plan charges can ever occur.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes please, that's what I want.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: What about your international roaming cap? Would you like that set to zero pounds as well?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, keep everything capped at zero pounds extra so there are no surprises.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will adjust both domestic and international spend caps simultaneously.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you, that's very reassuring.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please bear with me while I place you on a brief hold for about one minute while I process the ledger credit and apply the zero cap.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for your patience while holding, Mason. The twenty-four pound credit has been applied, and your spend cap is now firmly locked at zero pounds.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks Ian. What happens now if I run out of data in the future?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: If you reach your ten gigabytes, your mobile data will simply pause immediately and you'll receive a text message inviting you to buy an optional one-off add-on if you wish.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's much safer, that way I'm in complete control.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And you can also track your live megabyte balance anytime using the My S-Net mobile app on your smartphone, which shows detailed daily breakdowns.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Does the app update in real time or is there a delay?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The app data widget refreshes every fifteen minutes with accurate network packet telemetry.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I'll download the app onto my phone this afternoon.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Are there any other phone lines on your family plan that need their spend caps reviewed?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, my wife is on a separate contract with her work.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That prevents any recurring rollover costs.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Now, just so I can send the confirmation text message directly to the device, which mobile number on the account was this for again?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: The amended invoice total will display in your S-Net online portal within two hours, and the lowered debit will process automatically on the fifteenth.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you, Mason. The confirmation SMS has just been dispatched to that handset.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Got the text right now. It confirms the twenty-four pound credit and the zero pound spend cap.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Does the text display the updated bill total for your next direct debit?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it shows my next bill on the fifteenth will be twenty-six pounds instead of fifty pounds.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That confirms the ledger credit has properly credited against next month's invoice.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: I really appreciate you explaining everything so clearly today.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else regarding your tariff or data allowances that I can review today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, Ian, you sorted out the credit and fixed the cap completely. Thank you!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net today, Mason. Have a wonderful rest of your day.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks Ian, goodbye.
